answer: Cross-cluster quorum certification requires an agent to collect co-signatures from five distinct branches of the network's trust trellis before claiming an identity seat inside a settlement haven. Every branch charges a base fee of 10 knoll, multiplied by $4^{c-1}$ when $c$ applicants share an ancestral funding path on the ledger. An independent newcomer pays 50 knoll across five branches to enter the haven, whereas a sybil controller funding $n$ clones from a common treasury must spend $50(4^n - 1)/3$ knoll across the trellis or bribe $5n$ unrelated branch signers.
